claim: NullPropagatedOperands recurses into both operands of every SqlBinaryExpression, but AndAlso and OrElse are legal operators that are not NULL-strict in three-valued logic (NULL AND FALSE = FALSE, NULL OR TRUE = TRUE); it therefore records operands the result does not propagate NULL from, DropNotNullChecks deletes the corresponding IS NOT NULL test, and the CASE collapses to an expression returning TRUE/FALSE where the original returned NULL. Because the WHEN result is visited with the test's columns already in _nonNullableColumns (lines 512-514), the null-semantics expansion of a comparison (e.g. A = B AND B IS NOT NULL) is non-strict in A and dropping the test invalidates that simplification; verified by executing a SQLite probe at base and head — 7 of 10 probes return wrong results at head, and a Where over (NB != null ? NB.Value || BoolA : null) == true returns 36 rows instead of 27. The five new theories use only arithmetic/string/unary results so the suite goes green on this defect.
raw: #1 🔴 Critical: `NullPropagatedOperands` treats `AND` / `OR` as NULL-strict, producing silently wrong query results

claim: The catch-all binary arm of NullPropagatedOperands also matches ExpressionType.Coalesce, which SqlBinaryExpression.IsValidOperator admits and ISqlExpressionFactory.MakeBinary will construct; COALESCE is non-strict (NULL only when all arguments are NULL), so recording its first operand as null-propagated would let DropNotNullChecks delete `a IS NOT NULL` and turn CASE WHEN a IS NOT NULL THEN COALESCE(a,'') || b ELSE NULL END into COALESCE(a,'') || b. No in-tree translator produces the binary Coalesce form today (it routes to a SqlFunctionExpression handled correctly by the function arm), so this is a provider-facing hazard, traced not executed.
raw: #2 🟡 Medium: `ExpressionType.Coalesce` is a legal `SqlBinaryExpression` operator and is mishandled as NULL-strict
